claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing an apprenticeship in Wales - he's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify an important detail:

Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Wales? And do you know how many hours per week he works as part of his apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's in Wales - he travels there for it. As for the hours, he works full-time as part of the apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to understand a bit more about the apprenticeship structure:

When you say he works full-time, approximately how many hours per week is that? And is this a formal apprenticeship program recognized in Wales?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a proper formal apprenticeship program in Wales. When I say full-time, I mean he's there the standard working week - so that would be around 35 to 40 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's the assessment:

Since Alex is 17 years old, lives at home with you, and is undertaking a formal apprenticeship program, you continue to qualify for Child Benefit. The important point here is that the rule which would stop Child Benefit - where a child starts working 24+ hours per week in an apprenticeship - specifically applies only to apprenticeships **in England**. 

Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Wales, this exclusion doesn't apply to him. As long as he's under 20 and remains in approved training, you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit entitlement?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and still lives at home with the claimant, who is responsible for him. Although Alex has started an apprenticeship in Wales working 35-40 hours per week, the rule about losing Child Benefit specifically states that a child working 24 hours or more per week loses eligibility when they start 'an apprenticeship in England'. Alex's apprenticeship is in Wales, not England. Therefore, this specific exclusion does not apply to Alex. As Alex is under 20 and in approved training (a formal apprenticeship program), the claimant continues to qualify for Child Benefit for him.
